title: WPPIL/49/2017 of Upendra Kumar Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
WRIT PETITION (PIL) NO. 49 OF 2017
Upendra Kumar ....Petitioner.
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others. .......Respondents
Mr. B.S. Adhikari, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. C.S. Rawat, Additional Chief Standing Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand /
respondent nos. 1 & 2.
Mr. Arvind Vashisth, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. Ashish Sinha, Advocate holding
brief of Mr. Sandeep Kothari, Advocate for respondent no. 3.
Mr. Siddharth Bisht, Advocate for respondent no. 4.
Mr. Narendra Bali, Advocate for the intervener.
Dated: 07.10.2017
Coram: Hon'ble K.M. Joseph, C.J.
 Hon'ble Alok Singh, J.
K.M. Joseph, C.J. (Oral)
 This is a public interest litigation filed by a person, who
is admittedly a Member of the 3rd respondent Municipal Corporation
as the counselor. He calls in question two resolutions, namely,
Resolution dated 08.03.2016 and 19.04.2017.
2. The facts leading to the litigation can safely be
summarized as follows:
 There is a road known as 'Railway Station Road'. In the
year 1986, there was encroachment on the public utility land, namely,
a drain, which is maintained by the Public Works Department, by
certain persons. A writ petition was filed, which led to Annexure-1
judgment. According to the petitioner, the Hon'ble Apex Court has
directed that sixty persons before the Hon'ble Supreme Court, who
had approached the Court under Article 32 of the Constitution of India,
will deliver vacant possession of the respective shops in their
occupation to the Municipal Authorities on or before 30.06.1990.
The Municipal Authority was directed to provide temporary
accommodation to the surrendering shop-keepers at such place or

2
places as is / are convenient to the Municipal Authorities, for a term of
six months from 1st of July, 1990 till 31st of December, 1990 to carry
on their business. It was also directed that care shall be taken not to
prejudice the interest of the petitioners by the shifting. It was also
directed that every petitioner shall by 15.06.1990 deposit with the
Municipal Authorities a total amount of Rs. 20,000/- which would be
taken as contribution plus premium for being provided with the
constructed accommodation. There are other conditions also. It is
the further case that thereafter, there was a contempt petition by the
persons, who were affected on the ground that the order of the
Hon'ble Apex Court was not being complied with.
3. In fact, learned counsel for the intervenor Mr. Narendra
Bali would point out that there was initially an order that in view of
the reluctance of the Railway to give consent in the shops being
located, which according to the counsel for the Railway, are to be
located on the boundary on its property, the encroachers should not be
removed. Subsequently, it appears that the encroachers were removed
and thereafter, in contempt proceedings, Annexure 2 order was passed,
relevant portion of which reads as under:
 "Be that as it may, we are satisfied that pursuant to
the directions issued by this Court, the Municipal
Committee as also the State has framed a scheme for
accommodating the petitioners and, therefore, orders
passed by this Court stand complied with. However, if
for any reason, the petitioners are not satisfied with the
scheme framed, it would be open to them to seek
redressal in accordance with law. We direct that subject
to the petitioner's complying with the terms and
conditions of the said Scheme, the possession of the
alternative sites shall be delivered to them within four
weeks of their complying with the said conditions."
4. Thereafter, the case of the petitioner is that some other
area was originally suggested, but that also did not work out.
Subsequently, it is the resolutions that have been passed. As per the
resolution, the complaint of the petitioner is that it is to be located at
the very same place, fromwhere the petitioners were originally evicted,

3
which was the subject matter of Annexure 1 order of the Hon'ble
Apex Court.
4. We heard Mr. B.S. Adhikari, learned counsel for the
petitioner and Mr. Arvind Vashisth, Senior Counsel appearing on
behalf of the 3rd respondent.
5. Learned Senior Counsel would draw our attention to a
judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Bihar Public
Service Commission and another vs. Dr. Shiv Jatan Thakur and
others reported in 1994 Supp (3) SCC 220. He would invite our
attention to paragraph 28 of the judgment:
"28. Shri R.K. Garg, Senior Advocate, who appeared
for Dr. Thakur, the petitioner in the writ petition, since
did not make any submission in support of the reliefs
sought in paragraphs (B) and (C) of the prayer in the writ
petition, we do not feel the need to consider them. Shri
Garg, we are inclined to think did not make any
submission in support of the reliefs sought inparagraphs
(B) and (C) obviously realizing that the allegations on
which those reliefs were founded, related to functions of
the BPSC, which could not have been disowned by the
BPSC's sitting member. Whatever that be, no member of
a Public Service Commission, in our considered view,
could be allowed to question the validity or correctness
of the functions performed or duties discharged b the
Public Service Commission as a body, while he was its
member. It ought be so for the simple reason that such
member must be regarded to be a party to the function
required to be performed or the duty required to be
discharged by the Public Service commission as a body
or institution, even though he might have been a
dissenting member or a member in a minority or a
member who had abstained from taking part in such
function performed or duty discharged. Discretionary
remedy vested in the High Court under Article 226 of the
Constitution cannot, therefore, be allowed to be invoked
by a member of the Public Service Commission to
question the correctness or validity of function performed
or duties discharged by the Public Service Commission
as a body or institution, according to well established
procedures."
6. He would, therefore, contend that the petition at the
instance of a dissenting member of the Council may not be

4
maintainable. He would further refer to Section 537 of the U.P.
Municipal Corporation Act, 1959 (hereinafter referred to as the
Act), which reads as under:-
"537. Power of State Government to suspend action
under this Act.-If the State Government is of opinion
that the execution of any resolution or order of the
Corporation or of any other Corporation authority or of
any committee or joint committee or sub-committee or of
any officer or servant of the Corporation or the doing of
any act which is about to be done or is being done by or
on behalf of the Corporation is in contravention of or in
excess of the powers conferred by this Act or of any
other law for the time being in force or has been passed
or made in abuse of any such power or is likely to lead to
a breach of the peace or to cause obstruction, injury or
annoyance to the public or to any class or body of
persons or danger to human life, health or safety or is
prejudicial to public interest, the State Government may,
by order in writing, suspend the execution of such
resolution or order, or prohibit the doing of any such act.
(2) A copy of such order shall forthwith be sent to the
Corporation by the State Government.
(3) The State Government may at any time, on
representation by the Corporation or otherwise, revise,
modify or revoke an order passed under sub-section (1)."
7. He would, therefore, contend that it is not as if there is no
remedy open.
8. We also heard the learned counsel for the intervener Mr.
Narendra Bali, besides learned counsel for the Railways Mr.
Siddharth Bisht.
9. Mr. Siddharth Bisht, learned counsel for the Railways
would, in fact, point out that as far as the Railway is concerned, it has
not given its no objection. It is admitted that the Railway was not
inclined to surrender the land. Learned counsel for the Railway would
further point out that there is a scheme for renovation of the boundary
of the Railway which is for the project Pradhan Mantri Tirth Uddhaar
Yojna and as per the resolutions, the shops would be located at the
boundary.

5
10. We also heard Mr. C.S. Rawat, learned Additional Chief
Standing Counsel.
11. Having considered the matter, we are of the view that in
view of the power with the Government under Section 537 of the Act,
we need not go into this question. Since there is wide power with the
Government in regard to the resolutions in terms of the provisions as
contained therein, we only direct that the Government will consider
the resolutions and take a decision on the same as per law, necessarily
after giving opportunity to the third respondent, within a period of six
weeks from today. Till such time a decision is taken by the
Government, the resolutions, which are impugned, will be kept in
abeyance.
12. The writ petition stands disposed of.
 (Alok Singh, J.) (K.M. Joseph, C.J.)
 07.10.2017 07.10.2017
Rathour
